sections.h2: Which Boyle County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three desks touch a Boyle County bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), at 859-238-1104, decides what the property is worth for tax purposes and processes exemptions. The Sheriff's Office, at 321 W. Main Street, Room 103 in Danville (859-238-1123), mails the bills and takes the money. The county clerk inherits any bill still open after the spring cutoff.

The clerk's delinquent-tax page spells out that the sheriff never puts a value on anything. A bill that looks too large is a PVA conversation, and the call is easiest before the check goes out.

  • Value, exemptions, name or mailing address on the bill: PVA.
  • Paying this year's bill or looking it up: Sheriff's Office.
  • Bills from prior years: County Clerk.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Boyle County itself?
sections.html:
Boyle County fills 183 square miles of central Kentucky around Danville, the county seat. Junction City and Perryville are the other two cities. The county dates to 1842, carved from Lincoln and Mercer counties, and Perryville was the site of the October 8, 1862 battle. Centre College stands in Danville. Neighbors are Mercer, Garrard, Lincoln, Casey, Marion and Washington counties. Business figures for 2022 give the county economy some scale: $725.7 million in retail sales and $471.6 million in health care and social assistance receipts.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 31,632 people, a 3.3 percent rise over the 2020 count of 30,614. For the 2020 to 2024 period, QuickFacts shows what a seller is up against:

  • Houses lived in by their owners have a middle value of $209,900, and 68.0 percent of units are owner-occupied.
  • Rent in the middle of the range is $778, spread over 12,045 households.
  • Household income in the middle is $61,159, and workers spend 21.3 minutes getting to work on average.
  • The county logged 94 building permits during 2025.

sections.h2: When are Boyle County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The sheriff publishes a ladder of five cutoffs for each tax year. The 2026 version is below, and a postmark on or before the date counts.

Boyle County Sheriff's Office schedule for the 2026 bills (source: boylecountyky.gov)
Paid or postmarked byAmount owed
November 30, 2026Face amount less a 2% discount
December 31, 2026Face amount
January 31, 2027Face amount plus a 5% penalty
April 15, 2027Face amount plus a 21% penalty
After April 15, 2027Handed to the County Clerk as delinquent

Each year repeats this pattern with the calendar moved forward. The sheriff's Tax Bill Web Portal searches by bill number, map number, owner or address. Owner searches sometimes fail on reversed names, so try Doe John as well as John Doe.

sections.h2: Which school district bills Danville properties?
sections.html:
Street by street. Boyle County has two districts: Danville Schools inside the city and Boyle County Schools everywhere else. A handful of parcels inside the Danville limits still sit in the county district, so a Danville mailing address proves nothing.

Danville's property tax page explains the effect. A parcel in the Danville Independent district receives its school bill straight from the school system (859-936-8507). A parcel in the county district has school tax included on the sheriff's bill. Library, health, fire and similar special districts show up as extra lines where they apply.

sections.h2: What is the Danville city tax rate per $100?
sections.html:
Danville's 2025 real property rate is 11.9 cents on each $100 of assessed value, compared with 14.4 cents in 2017. Kentucky's own rate was 10.6 cents in 2025. The city reports taking the compensating rate every year since 2017, so the rate slid while assessments grew.

  • Real property: 0.1190 in 2025, 0.1220 in 2024, 0.1440 in 2017.
  • Tangible personal property: 0.1595 in 2025.
  • Cars, trucks and boats: 0.2000 in 2025.

House Bill 44 lets a city hold revenue level with the compensating rate or raise it by up to 4 percent after a hearing. Beyond 4 percent, voters can petition to recall the increase. A dollar total can still climb when the PVA lifts the assessed value under a lower rate.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Boyle County assessment?
sections.html:
A conference at the PVA's office comes first, and Kentucky offers no way around it. Values are fixed as of January 1. The roll lies open to the public for thirteen days in early May. After a conference you file the appeal with the county clerk by the close of the workday that follows the last open day.

The local board of assessment appeals sits roughly a month later, for up to five days. It wants evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal, repair quotes, insurance values or listings. Without it the appeal fails. An owner who never files locally cannot move on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Where bills are printed before the dispute ends, they use your own claimed value, with a supplemental bill if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption?
sections.html:
An owner aged 65 and up, or classed as totally disabled by a public or private retirement system, can knock a set dollar amount off the assessment of the home where they live. The state's ceiling is $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Ownership and residence must both hold on January 1.

Applications go to the Boyle County PVA, which Danville names as the office for senior homestead questions. Send yours in before December 31. When your bill shows no exemption and you qualify, call the PVA before paying.

sections.h2: What happens when a Boyle County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After April 15 the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the clerk's office and a lien attaches to the property. Interest accrues monthly at one percent, and clerk and county attorney commissions, postage and advertising pile on. The state's sample turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 when it leaves the sheriff and roughly $1,388 within the first week at the clerk.

County attorney letters follow at about 30 and 60 days, and a sale of unpaid certificates to outside buyers can be set between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. A seller with old tax outstanding should ask the clerk for a payoff so the closing agent settles it from proceeds.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when a Boyle County house sells?
sections.html:
Kentucky bills whoever holds title on January 1. A house that changes hands in March still produces that year's bill in the seller's name. Closing agents normally split the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, then either pay the sheriff or give a credit to the party who will. A lender with an escrow account does not get a bill automatically, so owners should forward it.

Houses that arrive through an estate, carry back taxes, or need repairs a retail buyer would balk at can sell directly to a cash buyer and clear the tax at the same table. Get the current figure from the sheriff and the older figure from the clerk before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Boyle County assessment looks too high?
faqs.a: The PVA at 859-238-1104. The sheriff collects only, and the clerk handles appeal filings.

faqs.q: Is the Boyle County 2% discount still available after November?
faqs.a: No. On the 2026 bills the discount ran through November 30, 2026. December brings the face amount and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Do Danville homeowners get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: It varies. Parcels in the Danville Independent district get a separate school bill, while everything else, including Boyle County school tax, comes on the sheriff's bill.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The ceiling is $49,100 through the 2026 tax year, for owner-occupants aged 65 and up or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Boyle County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the clerk for a payoff on past-due bills and the sheriff for the current figure, then have the closing agent pay both from proceeds.
